issues.title: Skip redundant found-match stores in RIGHT/FULL join probe
issues.hypothesis: HASH_JOIN RIGHT costs 2.15s of operator CPU on q13, its second-biggest cost. The build side is 1.5M unique keys and 14.8M probe rows hit it, so each build row gets about 10 matches spread across 8 threads. In ScanStructure (src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp around line 1018-1027, inside the `PropagatesBuildSide(ht.join_type)` block), every match does an unconditional `Store<bool>(true, ptrs[idx] + ht.tuple_size)`. Each store is a write to a cache line that other cores hold in shared state. That forces an RFO/invalidation, so lines bounce between cores even though the flag is already true after the first match. The probe has just compared keys in that row, so the line is already in cache. Loading the flag first and storing only when it is false turns about 90% of these writes into cheap shared reads. The code already does this check-before-write in the RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI path (line 1145, `if (Load<bool>(ptr + ht.tuple_size))`), but the regular RIGHT/FULL path does not.
issues.plan: In src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp, inside the matching loop that marks build-side found flags for PropagatesBuildSide join types (the loop at about line 1021 with `Store<bool>(true, ptrs[idx] + ht.tuple_size)`), change it to: `auto loc = ptrs[idx] + ht.tuple_size; if (!Load<bool>(loc)) { Store<bool>(true, loc); }`. Also apply the same guard to the store at about line 1168 (the non-equality-predicate branch of the RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI path). Nothing else changes. Semantics are the same because the only value ever written is true. Build and run bench on q13. Then run EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare HASH_JOIN operator time (was 2.15s).
issues.expected_gain: q13: HASH_JOIN operator time could drop substantially if coherence traffic dominates. Estimate 5-12% wall time on q13.
issues.generality: Any RIGHT/FULL OUTER join (including LEFT joins flipped to RIGHT by the planner) where build rows match many probe rows across threads, such as fact-to-dimension outer joins. The cost is one extra predictable branch per match. A probe where every build row matches exactly once pays a tiny load+branch, which is negligible.
issues.risk: Very low. It is a 3-line change with identical semantics, and the same pattern already exists in the same file.

issues.title: Parallel/partitioned combine for perfect hash aggregate with large key range
issues.hypothesis: E0001 (perfect hash aggregate up to 22 bits, guarded by density) cut q13's inner aggregate operator time from 3.14s to 0.53s, but wall time improved only 3.6%. PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate::Combine (src/execution/operator/aggregate/physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp:164-172) merges each thread's full 2^bits table into the global table under a single mutex. With 8 threads x 2M slots, that is a serial phase of about 16M slot merges, and the source then scans the table on one thread. So most of the CPU saved is lost to serialisation.
issues.plan: Investigate first: profile E0001's variant (SET perfect_ht_threshold=22) and check whether the Finalize/Combine phase is the serial bottleneck. If it is, re-land E0001's CanUsePerfectHashAggregate heuristic and make the combine partitioned: split the slot range into ranges, and have each thread combine its own range from all local tables (for example via a Finalize event or a lock per range).
issues.expected_gain: q13: maybe 10-15% if the serial combine is the remaining gap (operator CPU fell by about 2.6s)
issues.generality: GROUP BY on dense integer keys with large ranges (ids, dates)
issues.risk: Medium: changes the parallel structure of the operator. Needs the memory guard from E0001.

## Memory (planner notes)

### Workload: q13 only (customer LEFT JOIN orders with NOT LIKE '%a%b%' filter, count per key, then count per count)
Operator CPU times on the baseline (total 1.08s under EXPLAIN ANALYZE, about 812-849ms hot):
- inner HASH_GROUP_BY (count, 15.3M rows -> 1.5M groups): 3.08-3.14s  <- biggest
- orders TABLE_SCAN with LIKE filter on an FSST string column: 2.78-2.97s
- HASH_JOIN RIGHT (build: customer keys, unique, 1.5M; probe 14.8M): 2.0-2.15s
- outer group by and order by: negligible. Compress/decompress projections: about 0.06s total.

### Facts learned
- CanUsePerfectHashAggregate: src/execution/physical_plan/plan_aggregate.cpp:127, gated by perfect_ht_threshold (default 12). Settings defaults are off limits.
- PerfectAggregateHashTable allocates outside the buffer manager (no spilling), so it needs a memory guard.
- PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate::Combine (physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp:164) merges whole local tables under ONE mutex, so it is serial. That likely explains E0001.
- Perfect hash join (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66 CanDoPerfectHashJoin): INNER only, a single condition, MAX_BUILD_SIZE=1048576 range. q13's join (RIGHT, range 1.5M) is excluded on both counts. Extending it to RIGHT needs a found-match bitmap plus a full-outer scan, which is a big change.
- RIGHT/FULL probe marks build found flags with an unconditional Store at join_hashtable.cpp about line 1026. The RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI path already does check-before-store (about line 1145).
- LIKE: LikeMatcher (src/function/scalar/string/like.cpp:225) is already segment + memchr based. The scan cost is likely FSST decode (see auto-memory).
- dbe-tool sql accepts "SET ...; EXPLAIN ANALYZE ..." for quick what-if tests.
- Acceptance needs at least -5% on q13 beyond noise. bench quick checks overstate gains (E0001: bench -8.3%, official -3.6%).

### Experiments
- E0001 dense-range perfect HA: RETIRED at -3.6% (below the 5% bar). It was a good idea, but the serial combine wasted the gain. It is not exhausted: retry it together with a partitioned/parallel combine (issue filed).
- Round 2 dispatched: conditional found-match store in the RIGHT join probe (avoids cache-line ping-pong).

### Directions
- Next: parallel combine + E0001 re-land; FSST-aware LIKE evaluation (hard); perfect hash join for RIGHT joins with a larger range (big).
